newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures close lower across board.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures close lower across board.

text.p: Singapore rubber futures closed lower across the board on Tuesday in moderate trade in line with lower Japanese prices, brokers said.
They said prices in Tokyo and Kobe were lower as sentiment was still dampened by the Asian currency crisis and concerns the Thai government may sell some of its rubber stocks.

"The morning session was untraded, but prices were marked down in the afternoon in sympathy with weaker prices in Tokyo and Kobe. There's still some nervousness about currency problems in the region and most traders were not willing to open or hold new positions," a local dealer said.
The market was also looking at the possibility Bangkok may be forced to sell some of its stocks soon as part of a rescue package with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"The talk is still going around the market," a dealer said. "It may take some time before it is cleared up."

At around 0945 GMT, January/March RSS3 fell 2.25 cents to 96.75 U.S. cents a kg. September RSS1 fell 1.25 cents to 136.75 Singapore cents (90.50 U.S. cents) a kg. October TSR20 FOB fell 1.25 cents to 91.00 U.S. cents a kg. (US$1=S$1.51)
